title: Galvanic Cell Electron Flow Simulator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D galvanic cell electron flow simulator using Three.js and GLTFLoader (from CDN). The scene simulates a Zn-Cu galvanic cell with electron flow, ion migration, and voltage tracking.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 14) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark navy).
- OrbitControls for camera interaction.

## 3D Asset Loading
- Load 'coffeemat.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to (2, 0.3, 3) and position at (0, -1, 0). This serves as the base platform / lab bench mat on which the galvanic cell sits.
- Load 'PrimaryIonDrive.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to (1.5, 1.5, 1.5) and position at (0, 2, -2). This represents the ion drive / salt bridge mechanism connecting the two half-cells.
- After both models load, set window.__3D_STATE__.modelsLoaded = true.

## Galvanic Cell Construction (built with Three.js primitives on top of the loaded models)
- Create two beaker-like containers (transparent cylinders, radius 1.5, height 3) positioned at (-3.5, 0.5, 0) for the Zn anode half-cell and (3.5, 0.5, 0) for the Cu cathode half-cell.
- Zn beaker: fill with a semi-transparent blue liquid (flat plane or short cylinder inside, color #4488cc, opacity 0.4). Cu beaker: fill with semi-transparent blue-green liquid (color #22aa88, opacity 0.4).
- Place a Zn electrode (gray box, 0.3x2.5x0.3) inside the left beaker and a Cu electrode (orange-brown box, 0.3x2.5x0.3) inside the right beaker.
- Draw a wire (TubeGeometry following a curved path) connecting the tops of both electrodes, passing over the PrimaryIonDrive model (the salt bridge).

## Electron Flow Simulation
- Create a pool of 20 small spheres (radius 0.08, color yellow #ffff00, emissive) representing electrons. Initially all parked at the Zn electrode.
- When simulation is running, electrons flow along the wire path from Zn (anode) to Cu (cathode) at a speed determined by the current resistance setting.
- Electrons move in a queue; when one reaches the Cu electrode, it resets to the Zn electrode to create a continuous loop.
- Track totalElectronsTransferred (increments each time an electron completes one full trip).

## Ion Migration
- Create 10 small green spheres (Zn2+ ions, radius 0.06) that slowly drift from the Zn electrode into the solution when simulation runs.
- Create 10 small red spheres (SO4^2- ions, radius 0.06) inside the salt bridge model area that drift toward the Zn half-cell.
- Track ionsMigrated count.

## Chemistry State
- Zn electrode mass starts at 65.38 (g). Each electron transfer event reduces it by 0.001g.
- Cu electrode mass starts at 63.55 (g). Each electron transfer event increases it by 0.001g.
- Cell voltage starts at 1.10V (standard Zn-Cu cell). As Zn depletes, voltage decreases linearly. If Zn mass < 60.0, voltage drops to 0 and simulation auto-stops.
- Maintain a running Faraday efficiency: (totalElectronsTransferred * 2 * 96485) / (theoreticalMax) — expose as faradayEfficiency (0 to 1).

## User Interactions
- A 'Start/Pause' button (DOM, id='btn-start') toggles simulation. Label changes between 'Start' and 'Pause'.
- A 'Reset' button (DOM, id='btn-reset') resets all state to initial values.
- A resistance slider (DOM, id='slider-resistance', range 1-10, default 5) controls electron flow speed. Higher resistance = slower flow.
- Keyboard 'R' key: same as Reset button.
- Keyboard '+' / '-' keys: increase/decrease resistance by 1 (clamped 1-10).
- Clicking on the Zn electrode (raycasting) highlights it and shows a tooltip with current mass.
- Clicking on the Cu electrode highlights it and shows its current mass.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (DOM overlay, id='hud') showing:
  - Cell Voltage (id='hud-voltage'): e.g. '1.10 V'
  - Electrons Transferred (id='hud-electrons'): integer count
  - Zn Mass (id='hud-zn-mass'): e.g. '65.38 g'
  - Cu Mass (id='hud-cu-mass'): e.g. '63.55 g'
  - Resistance (id='hud-resistance'): current slider value
  - Simulation Status (id='hud-status'): 'Stopped' / 'Running' / 'Depleted'
- Style the HUD with a semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font.

## window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
- modelsLoaded: boolean
- simulationRunning: boolean
- totalElectronsTransferred: number (integer)
- ionsMigrated: number (integer)
- znMass: number (starts 65.38)
- cuMass: number (starts 63.55)
- cellVoltage: number (starts 1.10)
- resistance: number (1-10, default 5)
- faradayEfficiency: number (0-1)
- electronPositions: array of {x,y,z} for each electron sphere
- selectedElectrode: string|null ('Zn', 'Cu', or null)
- simStatus: string ('Stopped', 'Running', 'Depleted')
- elapsedTime: number (seconds since simulation started, resets on reset)
- massConservationDelta: number (should be ~0; computed as |(znMassLoss) - (cuMassGain)|)

## Physics Constraints
- Mass conservation: znMassLoss must equal cuMassGain at all times (massConservationDelta < 0.001).
- Voltage must be non-negative and <= 1.10.
- All positions must be NaN-free.
- Electron count must remain exactly 20 at all times.
- Resistance clamped to [1, 10].
physics_constraints: Mass conservation: Zn mass loss must equal Cu mass gain (delta < 0.001). Cell voltage bounded [0, 1.10]V. All electron positions NaN-free. Electron count invariant at 20. Resistance clamped [1,10]. Faraday efficiency in [0,1].
